perspective:
I am Brandon Talayumptewa, an Alaska Native insurance agent with a bachelor’s degree and an ISTP personality.

I met Benjamin Erickson, a white man and entrepreneur, when he sought business insurance advice. I knew he had limited formal education, so I was concerned about explaining complex insurance details clearly.

First meeting: I heard Benjamin say he wanted comprehensive coverage and that some terms were new. I explained liability insurance as a safety net, using the example of someone slipping and falling in his store. He said that made sense, asked for an example, said it simplified things, and asked about assets. I explained asset protection as covering inventory and equipment, like a guard over physical investments. He said he got it and thanked me.

Second meeting: I had revised my belief about his ability to understand details; I felt confident and planned to discuss more complex options. Benjamin said he was ready and had been reading up since our last meeting. I explained business interruption insurance as covering income loss when he can’t operate normally, and property insurance as covering damages and theft losses. He said these sounded crucial and reassuring.

Lunch meeting: I worried I was too detail-focused and wanted to be more engaging. Benjamin said he appreciated my thoroughness but also enjoyed lighter moments. I told the joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds for a million dollars. He found it fascinating and connected it to stakes. I said it was about assessing unique risks, like his business but less unusual. He agreed.

Later meeting: Pleased by his response, I decided to offer support beyond insurance. Benjamin said my insights were invaluable. I suggested strategic investments and security upgrades that could lower premiums. He called it smart and a win-win, and agreed to explore it.

Joint venture discussion: Encouraged by our collaboration, I proposed co-developing a platform integrating risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. Benjamin agreed it was groundbreaking and suggested drafting initial plans.
